operations.description: Deletes a key and the data associated with it. The key is removed and no longer counts against the key quota. Note that since this method is not safe in the face of concurrent modifications, it should only be used for development and testing purposes. Invoking this method in shipping code can result in data loss and data corruption.
operations.T: [METHOD] delete [NAME] appstate states delete [PATH] states [PARAMS] alt fields ip key oauth pretty print quota state token user [SCHEMA]

operations.description: Lists all the states keys, and optionally the state data.
operations.T: [METHOD] get [NAME] appstate states list [PATH] states [PARAMS] alt data fields include ip key oauth pretty print quota token user [SCHEMA] list response

operations.description: Retrieves the data corresponding to the passed key. If the key does not exist on the server, an HTTP 404 will be returned.
operations.T: [METHOD] get [NAME] appstate states [PATH] states [PARAMS] alt fields ip key oauth pretty print quota state token user [SCHEMA] response

operations.description: Clears (sets to empty) the data for the passed key if and only if the passed version matches the currently stored version. This method results in a conflict error on version mismatch.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] appstate states clear [PATH] states clear [PARAMS] alt current data fields ip key oauth pretty print quota state token user version [SCHEMA] result write

operations.description: Update the data associated with the input key if and only if the passed version matches the currently stored version. This method is safe in the face of concurrent writes. Maximum per-key size is 128KB.
operations.T: [METHOD] put [NAME] appstate states update [PATH] states [PARAMS] alt current fields ip key oauth pretty print quota state token user version [SCHEMA] request result update write
